answer: Sybil resistance rests on bonded identity, not cheap accounts: each agent posts stake slashed once an attestation proves false. A farm of duplicates sits at its economic nadir, since every fake identity raises the capital an attacker risks while adding no independent trust. Honest agents wander across tasks and build history that cannot be transferred, and voting weight is capped per proof-of-personhood — a narrow jetty, not an open door. Buying quorum then costs real slashable collateral across many distinct humans, more than the reward it captures.
